name: AdPact
try_it:
AdPact is a decentralized, AI-powered creator sponsorship marketplace on GenLayer that replaces payment delays (Net-30/60) and mutual distrust with an intelligent escrow state machine.

Creators link their X account via cryptographic challenge tweets, gaining an on-chain AI Trust Score cross-verified with Sorsa (app.sorsa.io) and TwitterScore.

Advertisers lock campaign funds in escrow upfront. When a creator publishes, GenLayer validator nodes scrape the live post and use LLM consensus to verify text, keywords, and hashtags against the pre-approved draft—triggering an immediate initial milestone payout.

Crucially, AdPact enforces an autonomous retention monitoring period: validator nodes continuously monitor the post to verify it remains live and unaltered throughout the agreed window (e.g. 24h–7d). Only when retention check passes is the final milestone released, fully protecting sponsors against post-and-delete fraud.

name: AffiliateGuard
try_it:
AffiliateGuard is a trustless affiliate escrow platform powered by GenLayer Intelligent Contracts. Brands escrow funds and set campaign terms, while creators deposit a mandatory 20% stake. 

GenLayer Multi-Agent LLM consensus nodes automatically audit video submissions using strict canonical domain parsing, audio transcript verification, and non-inference visual rules, releasing payouts or arbitrating disputes without central intermediaries.

name: AgentVault
try_it: A principal writes a spending mandate in plain English, names the agent wallet, lists allowed recipients, and sets a total budget, per-action cap, action limit and expiry. When the agent proposes a payment, deterministic checks run first. GenLayer validators then decide whether the described action fits the mandate. AUTHORIZED transfers native GEN in the same transaction; DENIED transfers nothing but still consumes an action slot. The model never chooses the amount. The principal can revoke the mandate and withdraw any unspent GEN.

name: Agent Work Order
try_it: Agent Work Order is bilateral escrow for agent jobs on GenLayer. A client names an agent, writes a checkable spec, allowlists trusted domains, sets a deadline, and locks GEN. The agent submits a public HTTPS URL. Equivalence validators fetch the live page and agree on a boolean: met_spec. Pass pays the agent immediately. Fail holds the bounty, the agent may appeal once with a bond within 24 hours and after the window anyone can finalize and refund the client. A missed deadline expires back to the client. Malformed LLM judgments do not move money.

name: AI Dispute Resolution
try_it:
An escrow-backed dispute resolution dApp built on GenLayer. A plaintiff funds an escrow to open a dispute against a defendant, submitting an evidence URL. The defendant may submit counter-evidence. An AI arbitrator fetches both parties' evidence and reaches a consensus verdict before releasing the escrow.

How it works:
- Open a dispute with a description and evidence URL (funds the escrow)
- The defendant submits counter-evidence
- resolve_dispute fetches evidence via gl.nondet.web.render and validators agree on the verdict (PLAINTIFF / DEFENDANT / INCONCLUSIVE)
- The escrow is released to the winner; if evidence is missing, it is returned to the plaintiff

Consensus: gl.eq_principle.prompt_comparative binds the verdict and which party's evidence was actually retrieved, so validators agree before funds move.

For freelancers, marketplaces, and escrow services that need neutral, evidence-based dispute settlement without a trusted middleman.

name: MilestoneProof — Verifiable On-Chain Milestone Evidence
try_it: MilestoneProof is a backend-free GenLayer application for open-source grants and milestone-based delivery. A sponsor freezes the builder, ordered acceptance criteria, allowed evidence sources, and deadlines in an intentionally frozen Intelligent Contract. The builder submits public repository, release, CI, or deployment evidence. GenLayer validators compare that evidence with every frozen criterion and return APPROVED, REJECTED, REQUEST_MORE_INFO, or UNRESOLVED. Authorization, replay protection, attempt limits, deadlines, state transitions, and authoritative readback remain deterministic and on-chain. Neither sponsor nor builder can unilaterally choose approval, and uncertain or invalid evidence never defaults to success. The production UI exposes wallet-indexed projects and shows transaction success only after finalized execution and contract readback.

name: AIEscrowArbiter
try_it:
AI Escrow Arbiter is an intelligent-contract escrow that settles disputes with AI instead of a human middleman. A buyer deploys an EscrowArbiter contract from the browser, setting the seller, amount, and release terms, then funds it with real GEN held in trust. Either party can submit evidence (text or links) on-chain while the escrow is funded. Calling resolve() triggers GenLayer validators to run an AI arbiter that reads the terms and evidence, reaches consensus on a verdict — RELEASE (pay the seller) or REFUND (return the buyer) — and records a written reason. payout() then releases the funds accordingly.

The frontend is a full Web3 dApp: EIP-6963 wallet connection, auto network switch to Testnet Bradbury, browser deployment, funding, evidence submission, AI resolution, and payout — every step an on-chain transaction with an Explorer link.

name: Air Disruption Cause Ledger
try_it: Air Disruption Cause Ledger lets travelers and support teams register one exact flight, route, date and UTC disruption window, then bind official carrier, FAA and weather URLs to that immutable case. GenLayer validators independently render the sources, classify each as BOUND, UNBOUND or UNAVAILABLE, compare the material evidence and store a consensus signal with digests, grounded excerpts and an explanation. The app fails closed to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when official pages do not prove the flight and window. Users can run a provisional assessment, add an eligible BTS or FAA ASPM revision source when review is required, and reload the public on-chain result without connecting a wallet.

name: AirJudge
try_it: AirJudge is a GenLayer dApp for contribution-based reward campaigns. Campaign creators define qualitative eligibility criteria and fund a GEN reward pool. Applicants submit a public proof page and contribution evidence tied to their wallet. GenLayer validators verify the proof-to-evidence binding and use consensus to decide whether the contribution satisfies the campaign criteria. Eligible rewards are reserved onchain and can then be claimed by the applicant. AirJudge is designed for communities, grants, hackathons, and ecosystem programs that need transparent, verifiable, and automated contribution review without relying on a single centralized reviewer.

name: Alpha Court: Reputation Court for Staked Crypto Theses
try_it: Alpha Court is an on-chain prediction court on GenLayer for staked crypto market theses (price, relative performance, fundamentals). Claims lock structured Surf evidence; GenVM validators reach consensus on HELD/BROKEN with deterministic arithmetic cross-checks.

name: AppAudit
try_it:
AppAudit lets a privacy advocate challenge an app's privacy claims against its own store listing. The advocate stakes GEN and names the claim. The app developer responds and counter-stakes. GenLayer validators independently fetch the Google Play Data Safety or App Store App Privacy section and judge whether the listing contradicts the claim.

GenLayer is used only for semantic interpretation of the privacy section against the stated claim. All settlement splits, contest bonds, default judgments, and withdrawals are deterministic arithmetic.

Seven outcomes on studio-dev: WhatsApp CONTRADICTED (listing declares location), Instagram VERIFIED, Spotify INCONCLUSIVE, TikTok contested and held, Facebook defaulted, Telegram withdrawn, Snapchat stalled and settled while paused. Every payout claimed, ledger balanced at zero.

Silence is never evidence , a listing that never mentions the claimed data type can only produce INCONCLUSIVE.

name: Arbiq - AI-Enforced Freelance Marketplace on GenLayer
try_it:
Arbiq is built on GenLayer, a blockchain that runs Intelligent Contracts: Python smart contracts that can call LLMs and reach non-deterministic consensus across independent validators. Arbiq uses this to have AI evaluate freelance work and automatically settle payment without a trusted third party.

When a client posts a job, their GEN tokens lock into the contract immediately. When the freelancer submits evidence of completed work, the client triggers an AI evaluation multiple GenLayer validators independently read the job spec and evidence URL, compare results, and if they agree, execute payment atomically. No cut, no human arbiter, no payment delays.

name: AuditBounty
try_it:
Web3 teams publish bounty tables, then grade their own reports. Hunters cannot force payment at the advertised severity. AuditBounty holds real GEN in one Intelligent Contract. An operator creates a program with scope, severity criteria, and four fixed payouts (Critical / High / Medium / Low), locking GEN into the pool. A hunter submits a report plus at least two independent reference URLs.

GenLayer AI consensus classifies the report into exactly one of five discrete verdicts: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or INVALID. Payout is a lookup of the amount published at create time — no percentages, no rounding. INVALID pays nothing. Validators compare verdicts with absolute equality, so two validators cannot "agree" while settling two different amounts.

AuditBounty does not work without GenLayer: no EVM contract can read an unstructured security report, and no third party is cheap enough to referee every small finding. Only decentralized AI consensus can do this at near-zero cost.

name: AuditMatch
try_it: AuditMatch is a GenLayer-native security-auditor matching application. Projects atomically publish immutable audit briefs and fit criteria. Auditors submit wallet-bound public evidence and conflict disclosures. GenLayer validators independently fetch and assess cited sources, producing expiring results with verdict, confidence BPS, independent-signal count, reason codes, and citations. Projects and integrations use deterministic evaluate_policy_view reads to enforce selection without an LLM at query time. Rechecks and contests preserve history. The corrected cross-platform expiry regression and 12-test direct suite pass on Ubuntu; the same public CI run verifies that the repository source and 25-method schema match the finalized StudioNet deployment.

name: AuditorShield — Decentralized Bug Bounty Court powered by GenLayer AI Consensus
try_it:
AuditorShield is a decentralized bug bounty court that automates the verification and payout of security vulnerability reports. Designed for Web3 projects and whitehat hackers, it eliminates slow, centralized, and expensive manual triaging processes.

By utilizing GenLayer's unique Intelligent Contracts, AuditorShield features:
- **Anti-Rugpull Guard**: Periodically monitors target code repositories; if code links are deleted or modified post-submission, it triggers automatic escalation to protect whitehat researchers.
- **Anti-Spam Verification**: Automatically renders submitted reports and verifies target URLs before executing deep LLM consensus.
- **GenVM AI Adjudication**: Executes multiple LLM-based security auditor agents in consensus to output whitelisted verdicts (PAYOUT, PARTIAL, REJECT, ESCALATE) and clamps confidence results.
- **Secure Escrow**: Automatically handles payouts (100% or 25% consolation/75% owner refund split) or resets the bounty safely upon rejection.

name: Aura
try_it:
Aura is a GenLayer contract where a freelance delivery-cadence agreement is re-judged by validator consensus every interval, for as long as it runs -- not resolved once, at the end, like a typical escrow or oracle contract. A client escrows the full project budget and a freelancer posts a bond sized exactly to the worst case (bond_per_interval x strike_threshold). Every interval, anyone can permissionlessly trigger a real consensus round: validators fetch the committed evidence source live and judge DELIVERED, MISSED, or INSUFFICIENT_DATA against a plain-English cadence rule.

A MISSED verdict doesn't pay out instantly -- it arms a bonded dispute window, so a single interval's ruling can be contested with fresh evidence without reopening the whole agreement's already-settled history. The dispute panel reads a recorded snapshot, never the live web again, so neither side can edit a page after the other has answered it.

name: AgentSLA
try_it:
AgentSLA is a GenLayer Intelligent Contract that brings trustless SLA
enforcement to the agentic economy. When one AI agent hires another to
complete a task, AgentSLA evaluates the delivered work against the
agreed contract terms using multi-step LLM reasoning — fetching evidence
from URLs, comparing it against stated requirements, and producing a
structured verdict (excellent/acceptable/partial/failed).

Payouts are graduated based on verdict, not binary: agents are paid
proportionally to quality, clients are refunded proportionally to
shortfall, and a small platform fee is collected. Agent reputation
updates on-chain after every resolved task, gating access to future
tasks.

Security-hardened: closed a fund-drain trust hole in task resolution and
fixed two non-functional withdrawal paths, all regression-tested (42
tests) and live on Studionet.

name: AutoProof
try_it: AutoProof is a bounty payment platform for developers with autonomous AI verification, built on GenLayer with USDC payouts on Base Sepolia via a LayerZero bridge. A sponsor funds a bounty and defines the criteria, backing it with reserved USDC up front. Any developer submits a GitHub repository, and a GenLayer AI judge reads the code and reaches a verdict through validator consensus. If the work meets the criteria, payment is released cross-chain to whoever submitted it, held in a settling state until confirmed on Base. If not, it is rejected. No human reviewer, no oracle: the network itself decides whether the work is real. It fails closed when source cannot be inspected, and settlement is restricted to the actual submitter.

name: Backfill
try_it: Backfill funds completed public-goods and maintenance work. Each epoch defines a scope, evidence requirements, cutoff, claim window, and challenge window. Contributors submit claims with independent HTTPS evidence. The Backfill Intelligent Contract fetches those sources through GenLayer nondeterministic execution, validates structured eligibility and impact fields across validators, records bounded retryable failures, supports counter-evidence challenges, and finalizes deterministic claim weights. A separate pool contract accepts native GEN, finalizes the allocation, and emits exact-once payout or refund transfers. The production app reads authoritative rounds and pool state and preserves transaction hashes, finality, execution results, and canonical readbacks. Current live evidence covers epoch creation, opening, 1 GEN funding, funder-credit reconciliation, and terminal inconclusive retry handling.

name: BenchmarkClaimProof
try_it: Benchmark Claim Proof checks one frozen public AI performance claim against one cited MLPerf Inference v6.0 result. Its GenLayer Intelligent Contract verifies the public source, pinned MLCommons commit, exact result row and configuration, then asks validators to judge whether the claim preserves the benchmark's scope and qualifications. The on-chain outcome is SUPPORTED, QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED, OVERSTATED, NOT_COMPARABLE or UNRESOLVED. Buyers, analysts and procurement teams can inspect the immutable evidence binding and assessment history without relying on a vendor's interpretation. GenLayer is essential because deterministic code can match identifiers, but semantic comparison of natural-language marketing claims with benchmark evidence requires web access, model reasoning and validator consensus. V1 does not rerun benchmarks, rank systems or certify vendors.

name: BenchSeal — Consensus-Certified AI Benchmark Provenance on GenLayer
try_it:
BenchSeal lets AI researchers publish tamper-proof model benchmark results on GenLayer. Labs submit their run by committing SHA-256 digests of four evidence pieces the rubric, task manifest, run manifest, and sample bundle  before scoring begins. GenLayer validators independently score the structured task-output pairs against the committed rubric and must reach consensus before a result is sealed.

The contract enforces: every sample task_id exists in the committed task manifest; no duplicate tasks; sample count meets both an absolute floor (min_samples) and a proportional floor (sample_rate x manifest size) so cherry-picking a small easy subset is impossible. The run manifest supports an attestation_url and attestation_digest for authenticated execution provenance both are committed on-chain and visible to validators during scoring.

No single party controls the outcome. The score is immutable once sealed.

name: BIBET
try_it: BIBET funds completed work based on evidence of real public impact. Contributors submit completed projects with public evidence, and GenLayer validators independently fetch and assess that evidence for eligibility, quality, attribution, duplication risk and impact. The contract then converts the agreed verdict into a deterministic impact score and capped allocation from a funded GEN round. BIBET also supports review deadlines, evidence commitments, challenges and re-adjudication, permissionless expiry of unreviewed claims, contributor claims, and withdrawal of unallocated funds. The result is a transparent retroactive-funding workflow where semantic judgement happens through GenLayer, while deadlines, accounting, caps, allocations and settlement remain deterministic and auditable on-chain.

name: Bidframe
try_it: Bidframe is a security-deposit settlement system built on GenLayer. A landlord registers the property inventory, move-in evidence, deposit amount and item-level deduction limits before the tenant funds the agreement. At checkout, move-out evidence is submitted and GenLayer validators compare the before-and-after images to classify the result as UNCHANGED, NORMAL_WEAR, NEW_DAMAGE, MISSING or INCONCLUSIVE. The AI only determines the condition and severity. It cannot choose prices or recipients. Deduction amounts are taken from the schedule frozen before funding, and the contract settles the final landlord payment and tenant refund in GEN. Bidframe also hash-binds evidence, supports challenges and fail-closed outcomes, and prevents repeat settlement.

name: BountyCourt
try_it:
A poster opens a bounty with acceptance criteria in plain English and escrows the reward in the same call. A hunter claims it by submitting a URL pinned to an immutable commit SHA - a branch reference can change between submission and adjudication, so it is refused. adjudicate() has every validator rule on every criterion independently, returning booleans only.

Consensus is required per criterion, not on a summary verdict, and the outcome is computed in deterministic code from the agreed booleans. Twelve checks run on the jury's output before any value moves.

The ruling does not pay out. It holds the escrow, so a verdict can be contested: the losing party stakes a bond equal to the escrow for a fresh jury. Overturned, they take escrow plus bond; upheld, both go to the other side.

If the artifact exceeds the readable window the contract returns INCONCLUSIVE rather than ruling.

name: BountyOracle
try_it:
BountyOracle is a trustless bounty escrow for open-source work. A maintainer locks GEN on a GitHub issue. A contributor claims with a PR URL. Anyone can trigger settlement.

Settlement runs inside the contract. It renders four pages on-chain — the issue, the PR, the diff, and CI checks — then asks an LLM for a verdict: ACCEPT, REJECT, or UNRESOLVABLE, with confidence and a rationale. Every validator independently re-reads GitHub and re-judges; the run succeeds only when they agree on the verdict, not the JSON shape. On ACCEPT above the maintainer's threshold, escrow releases automatically. On REJECT the bounty returns to OPEN. If pages cannot load it becomes UNRESOLVABLE and the maintainer may refund.

For OSS maintainers funding fixes without becoming sole judge, and contributors who want proof they will be paid the moment work is accepted. Solidity cannot fetch github.com or judge code — remove the on-chain web read and LLM and nothing is left to settle with.

name: Cadence
try_it:
Cadence is a non-custodial real-time payments platform built on Arc. A payer deposits USDC into a smart-contract stream, sets the payee, rate, and optional deliverables, and the payee earns continuously by the second. Payees can withdraw earned funds at any time, while payers can monitor runway, top up, or request cancellation. 

When a cancellation is disputed, the remaining escrow is held for a 24-hour appeal window. The payee can submit evidence, after which both parties enter a Bant room to exchange explanations and supporting evidence. GenLayer evaluates the deliverables, cancellation reason, submitted evidence, and Bant transcript, then relays a binary verdict back to the Arc payroll contract. This combines programmable payment streaming with decentralized adjudication for real-world payment disputes.

name: Campaign Ad Sponsor Trace
try_it: Campaign Ad Sponsor Trace is a public-record workbench for checking whether a political advertisement’s disclaimer can be mapped to the claimed FEC candidate and committee. A registrant submits the HTTPS artifact URL, its SHA-256 digest, exact disclaimer text, candidate ID, committee ID, election cycle, relation, observation time, and filing cutoff, then freezes the record. After the cutoff, GenLayer validators independently retrieve the artifact and official FEC/OpenFEC records and agree on a bounded evidence assessment. The contract preserves the frozen trace and immutable assessment revisions, including fail-closed unresolved outcomes when provenance or FEC evidence is unavailable. It does not determine legality, coordination, candidate quality, or proof of payment. Public traces are readable without a wallet; writes require an explicitly selected wallet on Studionet.

name: Chronix (Prediction Market Platform)
try_it: Chronix is a prediction market where markets can run for years, not days, and settlement is never a single party's call. Creators seed a market with a question, category, horizon, and resolution criteria; participants stake YES or NO with real GEN. When the deadline passes, on-chain and enforced, not by a backend cron, anyone can request adjudication. GenLayer validators then independently fetch real evidence across news, academic, and financial sources, classify it, and must derive the exact same verdict as each other, not just similar vote tallies, before a market settles YES, NO, or SPLIT. Failed fetches are excluded rather than counted as silent "neither" votes. Every payout, whether a settlement, a split, or a timeout refund when adjudication stalls, sends real GEN directly to each participant's wallet, zeroed from the ledger before the transfer so nothing can be claimed twice.

name: Claim Game
try_it:
ClaimGame is a Web3 strategy game where players interpret ambiguous protocol statements, back their interpretation with a GEN bond, and defend it against adversarial challengers backed by real evidence.

The verdict is never decided by a centralized server or a vote count. A GenLayer Intelligent Contract fetches the cited evidence live, normalizes and hashes it, and reasons over it, then requires independent validators to reach the same verdict through Optimistic Democracy before any GEN moves. Ledger balances are zeroed before any transfer, so a single choke point function is the only place funds ever leave through.

The backend and frontend are provably non-authoritative: the indexer only reads the contract, the API never writes claim state, and every fund-moving action is a direct wallet-signed transaction. If both were deleted, every dispute already onchain would still resolve correctly.

name: ClaimRegistry for GenLayer v3
try_it: ClaimRegistry is an interactive GenLayer application for durable, consensus-driven public claim checks. Users enter a claim plus two to five HTTPS sources from independent hosts, connect a Studio wallet, and create a new TreeMap-backed registry record. Each accepted write returns a unique check ID; the app then reads that exact record from the deployed contract to show the consensus verdict, provenance manifest, source-bundle commitment, observed snapshot hashes, submitter, and accepted-write binding. Validators agree on stable normalized source provenance and verdict structure, not character-exact dynamic webpage HTML.

name: ClausePilot — Living Commercial Contract Monitor
try_it:
ClausePilot turns natural-language commercial commitments into bounded, continuously monitored obligations.
An agreement owner registers a versioned agreement and clause digest, while the named counterparty must explicitly accept that exact record. The owner then defines an obligation, its authoritative source origin, exact evidence URL, bound object, observation window, and checkpoint cadence.
At each checkpoint, GenLayer validators independently fetch the authorized public evidence and use comparative AI consensus to classify the obligation as SATISFIED, AT_RISK, BREACHED, or UNRESOLVED. Deterministic contract logic verifies agreement identity, counterparty consent, source provenance, lifecycle state, observation sequence, and fail-closed behavior before any standing update is committed.

name: CleanCheckpoint – Privacy-Aware Cleaning Service Escrow
try_it: CleanCheckpoint is a decentralized escrow and dispute-resolution protocol for cleaning services. Clients lock service terms and payment, while providers post a bond and record append-only, role-bound checkpoints throughout the job. When both parties agree, the contract settles deterministically without AI. If they disagree, GenLayer validators evaluate the locked terms and submitted evidence to classify four bounded facts; the contract then calculates and executes the payout. Timed recovery paths protect both parties when someone becomes unresponsive or consensus cannot be reached. The live application connects directly to the deployed Intelligent Contract and exposes public on-chain job states without requiring a wallet.

name: Clearance
try_it:
Sample clearance takes months of label paperwork, so most remixers ship uncleared or never ship. Clearance replaces that with an on-chain adjudication.

An artist registers a track with licence terms in ordinary English ("4 seconds or less is free, 4-15 seconds needs 25%, no vocals, no alcohol ads"). A remixer submits their track URL, a declaration of how the sample is used, a proposed split, and a 0.01 GEN escrow. Adjudication is public: GenLayer validators fetch both track pages with gl.nondet.web.render, weigh the declaration against the licence, and reach consensus on APPROVED, MODIFIED or REJECTED plus a written rationale, recorded on-chain. MODIFIED overrides the proposed split with what the terms require.

Settlement pays the artist and refunds the escrow. A rejection forfeits it; the remixer can stake 2x to force one re-adjudication, capped at two.

Solidity cannot do this. It cannot read a SoundCloud page and cannot interpret "no alcohol ads".

name: Collara
try_it: Collara is reputation-backed credit on GenLayer. Instead of locking 150%+, borrowers link a public handle (X/GitHub/LinkedIn) via a proof_url that contains their wallet. Validators fetch proof_url + an independent source (api.github.com / unavatar.io) inside the contract and run LLM consensus (verified/handle_match/wallet_match then rubric 0–100) under Optimistic Democracy + Equivalence Principle (±12 + bucket, no oracle). The score sets collateral = principal*(150-score)% (50% at 100) and interest 12%→3%, with expiry = now+duration, value==collateral enforcement, and repay/liquidate guarded by now>=expiry. For retail borrowers who want capital efficiency without KYC, and lenders who want yield from filtered credit.

name: contentbounty
try_it: GenLayer Content Bounty is a trust-minimized platform for sponsors who want to commission verifiable web content and creators who want to earn rewards for completing bounties. Submissions are validated against creator-bound provenance signals and stable source content, while a 48-hour challenge window gives participants an opportunity to dispute an approved submission before the reward is released. This makes the payout process transparent, challengeable, and verifiable on-chain.

name: ContentScout — AI Content Originality Scanner
try_it: AI-Powered Content Originality Scanner deployed on GenLayer Studio Blockchain. Every score, verdict, and reasoning displayed in the UI comes exclusively from the on-chain AI consensus judgment — no browser-based heuristic is ever substituted.

name: Conveyance
try_it:
Conveyance is an escrow protocol for domain transfers.

A buyer locks GEN against agreed transfer terms. The seller accepts the deal, and GenLayer validators independently read authoritative registry RDAP data and two DNS resolvers to determine whether the domain moved to the agreed registrar, uses the agreed nameservers, and is under the buyer's DNS control.

Settlement is driven by those public facts rather than either party's word or a centralized escrow operator. The contract also handles deadlines, refunds, abandonment, reversal checks and value accounting.

Because the evidence is structured, Conveyance deliberately uses strict consensus rather than adding an LLM where one is unnecessary.

The production app reads and writes directly against the canonical StudioNet Intelligent Contract.

name: Counsel
try_it:
Counsel is a developer toolkit for building verifiable agreements and AI-assisted arbitration workflows. It is for developers, protocol teams, and agents that need safe coordination between principals, escrow contracts, oracles, and GenLayer validators.

It is useful because it combines demand drafting, oracle-neutrality checks, fulfilment review, human confirmation gates, model-based evaluation, arbitration, and receipt logging in one auditable workflow.

name: Courtscan
try_it:
A block explorer tells you a transaction finalised. It does not tell you whether the validators agreed, or whether the leader answered perfectly well and the round was thrown away. Those look identical there. One is a verdict; the other never happened.

Courtscan reads a round as a case record: who brought it, what they asked for, the claim read out of the calldata, what the leader proposed, how each validator voted, and whether it stands. The per validator votes are on chain and nothing else displays them.

Everything is a read. No wallet, no account, no GEN, so a stranger gets an answer as the page loads.

Beside it sits Assay, a contract running controlled rounds to find where agreement breaks. Every failure it reports is checked against its own receipt and the outcome taken from the chain rather than the label it was filed under. That is how a round filed as REVERTED turned out to be NO_MAJORITY: agreement actually breaking, at 3,500 characters with one bound field.

name: CROSS
try_it:
CROSS is a 1-hour prediction market where users choose which basket will perform better: US indices or FX.

The indices basket contains SPY, QQQ, and IWM. The FX basket contains EURUSD, GBPUSD, and USDJPY. Each basket is scored using the equal-weight average return of its three assets over the exact market window.

Settlement uses Gate and Bitget independently. Each source fetches all six candles and calculates its own winner. CROSS only settles when both sources agree. If consensus cannot be reached before the settlement deadline, the market becomes inconclusive and bettors can reclaim their original stake.

Users connect a wallet, choose INDICES or FX, place GEN, wait for the market to finish, then settle and claim winnings or a refund when applicable.

name: Crosschain Oracle v2 — Feed History & Staleness Detection
try_it:
Crosschain Oracle v2 is a decentralized oracle on GenLayer that aggregates and verifies data from multiple web sources. Each feed supports custom schemas and multiple source URLs; AI validator consensus (gl.eq_principle.prompt_comparative) extracts, normalizes, and cross-checks values across sources.

Key features:
- Feed creation with custom data schemas and multiple source URLs
- Multi-source AI consensus aggregation and normalization
- Feed history tracking: last 20 snapshots with timestamps
- Auto-staleness detection with configurable max age
- Deviation threshold monitoring across sources
- Confidence scoring with data quality warnings
- Per-feed SLA controls and freshness checks
- Subscriber system for consumers

Full dApp frontend supports the whole workflow: connect wallet, create a feed, update via AI consensus, check staleness, read the latest value, browse feed history, and subscribe.

name: Crown
try_it:
Crown is a permissionless relative-performance prediction market built on GenLayer. Each market asks which of BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, or XRP will achieve the highest percentage return over the same exact 4-hour UTC window.

Anyone can create a valid market, users stake GEN on one asset, and settlement is permissionless. Crown independently evaluates native 4-hour candles from Binance, Bitget, and Gate and requires at least 2 of 3 valid sources to agree before finalizing a result.

Winning positions share the pool pari-mutuel style. If Crown cannot safely finalize a payable winner, the market becomes inconclusive and participant stakes are refundable.

name: Crux
try_it: Crux is a decentralized evidence-completion market for unresolved decisions. Case sponsors open bounded questions with a GEN bounty and define two possible outcomes. Contributors submit public, checkable facts through a commit–reveal flow, keeping evidence private until it is committed on-chain. GenLayer validators independently inspect the cited source and fact, then reach consensus on whether the evidence makes the case decidable. Verified evidence resolves the case and routes the bounty according to the protocol rules. Crux is designed for teams, protocols, researchers, and communities that need transparent decisions grounded in public evidence rather than an operator’s private verdict.

name: Cryptographic Push Oracle
try_it:
The Cryptographic Push Oracle is an omni-chain intent routing infrastructure built on GenLayer. It solves a critical limitation in decentralized AI networks: the inability of strict VM sandboxes (like GenVM) to execute arbitrary web requests for live market data.

It aggregates live multi-chain telemetry (gas, liquidity, bridge security) via a Next.js frontend, canonicalizes the data, and secures it with a deterministic SHA-256 hash lock. This payload is pushed to a GenLayer Intelligent Contract, which mathematically verifies its integrity. Once verified, GenLayer’s multi-LLM consensus engine analyzes the live metrics against a user's natural language DeFi intent to dynamically calculate the optimal cross-chain route.

Built for DeFi traders, arbitrage bots, and cross-chain dApps, it is highly useful because it enables fully autonomous, AI-driven asset routing without relying on centralized oracles or risking GenVM determinism violations.

name: DataProof Market: AI-Juried Dataset Escrow
try_it:
DataProof Market lets a buyer lock real GEN behind a dataset request and a
fixed partial-payout policy. A provider submits content-addressed manifest,
sample, and license evidence. GenLayer validators independently assess semantic

name: DeliverableCourt
try_it:
DeliverableCourt is an AI-powered escrow platform on GenLayer that resolves subjective gig economy disputes. It issues deterministic verdicts (RELEASE, REFUND, ESCALATE) to fairly route locked funds. With built-in security that automatically locks the escrow if a client tampers with the brief, it provides trustless and automated dispute resolution without expensive human mediators.

name: Delivera (Performance Based Contracting Platfrorm)
try_it: Delivera puts freelance and agency payments into on-chain escrow that only releases when work is actually verified as delivered. Clients define milestones with concrete acceptance criteria and fund escrow; providers submit evidence as live URLs, never free-form claims. Disagreements go to AI arbitration with a basis-point split settlement rather than an all-or-nothing outcome. Every payout, whether a milestone approval, a dispute split, or a cancellation refund, sends real GEN directly to the recipient's wallet the moment it's earned. No party, including the platform itself, can decide a payout alone.

name: Dispute Court
try_it: Dispute Court helps clients and service providers resolve disagreements over delivered work without letting either side control the outcome. Party A funds; Party B performs. Both approve fixed terms and performance criteria before escrow is funded. EvidenceCaptureV4 captures public evidence and commits its digest; DisputeCourtV4 re-fetches sources and checks those digests before GenLayer consensus assesses performance. The contract maps five performance levels to payout shares and reason codes, rather than trusting model-generated amounts. A fixed chain-time deadline provides a fee-free 50/50 timeout exit. The wallet-only app tracks signed requests through finalization and verifies actual native payout delivery separately from withdrawal approval. This StudioNet release has public source, pinned dependencies, passing Ubuntu CI and a completed two-wallet resolution/withdrawal test. Test GEN only; not a legal court or mainnet-ready product, and not independently audited.

name: DomainArbiter
try_it:
DomainArbiter helps buyers and sellers arrange direct domain trades using smart-contract escrow. Sellers prove control of their domain by publishing a DNS TXT record. Buyers then deposit the agreed GEN amount into escrow before the domain is transferred.
GenLayer Intelligent Contracts verify public evidence and apply buyer-confirmation, deadline, dispute, and refund rules. Buyers can confirm receipt or prove their new DNS control, while unresolved issues follow the dispute process instead of automatically releasing funds.
Users can also create wallet-owned profiles with optional domain, X, or Reddit verification. Verifying both social accounts is not required.
The current release runs on StudioNet using test GEN. Domain transfers still take place through the domain registrar.

name: Dominion
try_it:
Dominion is a permissionless one-hour stock dominance market built on GenLayer. Users choose which stock in a fixed category they believe will deliver the strongest percentage return during an exact UTC hour and stake native GEN on that outcome.

Anyone can create a valid market, betting closes automatically when the hour begins, and anyone can trigger settlement after the window ends. Dominion reads independent index/reference-price candles from Binance, Bitget, and Gate. Each source determines its own winning stock, and a matching 2-of-3 result settles the market. Prices are never averaged across exchanges.

Winning positions share the total pool through pari-mutuel payouts with a 0% protocol fee. If reliable consensus cannot be reached, the market becomes inconclusive and bettors can reclaim their original stake. Dominion gives traders a simple, transparent way to express short-term views on relative stock performance without relying on a centralized resolver.

name: DrugClaimGuard
try_it: DrugClaimGuard addresses a trust gap in prescription-drug promotion: a public claim can be paired with the wrong application, product, dosage form, or label revision, while a centralized AI service creates another opaque decision-maker. Users register an HTTPS promotion URL, the exact claim and bounded context, then bind it to an FDA application/product and an exact DailyMed SPL version. GenLayer validators independently retrieve the bounded promotion and official label evidence, compare normalized identity and semantic fields, and store the resulting evidence signal, reason codes, source hashes, and revision history on-chain. Results are fail-closed and are not FDA findings, legal compliance determinations, medical advice, or treatment recommendations.

name: EOY
try_it:
EOY is an acceptance and settlement rail for work. A payer defines what “done” means and locks payment. A worker

name: Event-Weaver (Prediction Market Category)
try_it:
EventWeaver is an evidence-driven chain-reaction prediction market application built for the GenLayer ecosystem. It lets users create conditional markets with clear outcomes, a deadline, and one or more evidence sources that validators can inspect.
A market creator defines a question such as whether a real-world event will occur before a specific time. Participants stake USDC on YES or NO. The market outcome is not decided by a centralized operator. After the deadline or a resolution request, GenLayer validators evaluate the configured evidence sources and return an onchain verdict based on the stated market conditions.
EventWeaver separates decision making from asset custody. GenLayer stores market rules, participant positions, evidence steps, resolution status, and payout calculations. USDC staking and payment settlement happen on Base Sepolia through a dedicated ERC-20 escrow contract.

name: Evidence Desk — GenLayer dispute evidence console (in-repo ICs)
try_it:
Evidence Desk is a Next.js console where GenLayer is central to dispute evidence workflows.

IC sources ship in this repository (contracts/) with a method map to src/lib/contracts.ts. EN/UA UI, favorites, and CI included.

name: EvidenceQuorum — Auditable Consensus for Web Evidence
try_it:
EvidenceQuorum is a reusable GenLayer Intelligent Contract for public-web claims with conflicting sources. Submitters provide a claim and 2–8 distinct HTTPS URLs. The contract renders bounded source text, and leader plus validators independently assess it. It writes only SUPPORTED, REFUTED, or INCONCLUSIVE decisions. Each binary decision requires direct quotations from at least two material sources and agreement on the decision and material source/stance pattern.

The resulting on-chain dossier retains the decision, confidence, rationale, timestamp, source URLs, bounded captures, quotations, and challenge status. The React client reads canonical Studio state and requires an explicit wallet transaction before any attestation or challenge.

EvidenceQuorum supports governance, grant review, compliance, vendor due diligence, and event verification where inspectable evidence is needed.

name: EviFix
try_it: EviFix is a GenLayer-powered governance system for reviewing proposed changes to important contracts and applications. A patch is submitted with a candidate source, declared intent, scoped evidence and an immutable review policy. GenLayer validators independently interpret public evidence and determine whether the proposal satisfies the policy. Deterministic contract logic handles authorization, lifecycle rules, activation, escrow, refunds and settlement. EviFix is designed for teams that need transparent, evidence-based upgrades without relying on a single administrator or unverifiable approval.

name: FacilityClaim Ledger
try_it: FacilityClaim Ledger freezes a public environmental statement with its source URL, EPA FRS ID, program, and program identifier. Any visitor can submit a claim, then run a bounded 1,095-day ECHO assessment. GenLayer validators independently interpret the evidence and the contract appends one of SUPPORTED, QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED, CONTRADICTED, STALE_EVIDENCE, or UNRESOLVED with a reason code and evidence window. It is for compliance teams, facility operators, journalists, and community researchers who need an auditable record of what a public statement means within a defined scope. GenLayer matters because the semantic outcome is produced through independent validator consensus over live public records; a deterministic contract alone cannot interpret claim wording against changing, multi-record evidence. The result is a scoped signal, not a statutory finding, environmental-harm assessment, or legal opinion.

name: Factora
try_it: A business owed money on an invoice needs cash today; whoever advances it must trust evidence no price feed can verify. Factora makes that judgment on-chain. The seller commits each document as exact bytes, hashed into a manifest whose root freezes the record. The buyer's wallet countersigns the obligation on-chain (or files a dispute) - the one identity fact a seller cannot manufacture. A GenLayer validator panel judges the whole record: every validator independently re-reads the evidence and must agree on the decision, the risk class, the per-pillar findings, and the exact set of items examined. The model never touches money: a deterministic table keyed on the pinned risk class sets the advance and fee, a dispute filed after judgment strikes the terms until a fresh judgment reads it, and settlement is arithmetic - the split conserves to the atto and custody drains to zero. Proven live end to end on StudioNet, including the dispute arc.

name: ODDLOCK

name: Fieldwork - photo verified settlement for physical work
try_it:
Fieldwork settles payment for physical work on the evidence rather than on trust.

A poster writes an acceptance test in plain language, photographs the site as it looks now, and funds the task. The contract reads that acceptance test before the task can go live and refuses anything it could not judge from an image, so nobody funds work that no grader could assess consistently.

When a worker claims the task, the contract issues a six character code that cannot be known in advance. That code has to be legible in the photograph the worker takes, which is what ties the frame to that worker and that moment.

On submission the validators independently fetch both photographs and answer three questions: is the code visible, do both frames show the same place, and does the after frame meet the written standard. All three must be yes, and the validators must agree with each other, before the reward moves. The verdict and the transfer are the same transaction.

name: Find the Landmark — Multiplayer GenLayer Game
try_it:
Find the Landmark is a real-time lobby game for 2–50 players. A host creates a room and everyone plays the same 12-round match: five landmark image rounds, three atlas questions, and four questions sourced from the GenLayer Docs.

Each browser uses a temporary GenLayer signer to lock a salted answer commitment, preventing the relayer from changing a player’s choice. GenLayer transaction timestamps determine speed bonuses, validators check the committed evidence or authoritative source, and XP is awarded only after the round reaches finalized majority consensus.

Scores exist only within each game, and completed leaderboards can be reopened using the room code.

name: Flowed
try_it:
If the exact option is not available, use ConditFlowed is a funded sequential workflow built as a single GenLayer Intelligent Contract. A payer funds the complete job upfront and freezes 2–8 ordered steps, with an exact payment, acceptance criteria, evidence sources and timing attached to each step.

Only the active step can be reviewed. GenLayer evaluates whether the frozen public evidence satisfies that step's natural-language criteria. If satisfied, the result becomes provisional and can be contested by the payer with an exact 5% bond. A contest reuses the same stored evidence snapshot rather than fetching new evidence.

The model never chooses payment amounts, recipients, refunds or step ordering. Those remain deterministic contract rules.

Work moves. Money follows.

name: ForecastForge
try_it:
ForecastForge is a live forecasting protocol where participants create evidence-based markets and submit sealed predictions without exposing their choices during the commitment phase.

Each market moves through enforced on-chain phases for commitment, reveal, evidence collection, resolution, appeal, and finalization. GenLayer validators evaluate the submitted evidence against the market criteria and determine whether the outcome is YES, NO, or UNRESOLVED.

The production interface reads all market phases, forecasts, evidence, deadlines, outcomes, and reputation data directly from the deployed StudioNet contract. Every visible action sends a real wallet transaction and waits for an accepted or finalized result before refreshing authoritative contract state.

Evidence records support HTTPS sources, archived references, content hashes, and retrieval timestamps. A 48-hour appeal period requires new evidence, while unresolved markets remain neutral to participant reputation.

name: Fulfill
try_it:
Fulfill is a weighted performance escrow for commitments between a funder and a recipient.

The funder locks GEN before performance begins and freezes a scorecard containing the obligation, evidence catalogue, weighted checks, and scoped evidence sources. GenLayer validators independently interpret the permitted public evidence for each check and return SATISFIED, NOT SATISFIED, or UNRESOLVED.

GenLayer is used only for semantic evidence interpretation. All weights, percentages, contest bonds, payouts, refunds, recovery paths, and settlement calculations are deterministic on-chain.

Recipients earn the portion of escrow represented by satisfied check weights. Unused escrow returns to the funder. Either party can contest selected checks, while uncontested results remain unchanged.

name: GenArtAuth
try_it:
GenArtAuth verifies whether an artwork or NFT is original or a copy. The contract crawls the artwork page, its claimed sources, and Wayback Machine snapshots on-chain, then validator LLMs reach consensus on a verdict (ORIGINAL or COPY), an action (MINT_SAFE or BLOCK_MINT), a confidence score, and the earliest source. Anyone who disagrees can lock a 10 GEN stake and dispute it with new evidence; a second, deeper AI trial re-judges the case from forensic, provenance, and skeptic angles and pays out accordingly.

For NFT marketplaces screening mints, and artists needing a neutral record that their work came first.

A plagiarism ruling is a judgment call over unstructured web evidence: timestamps, archived pages, visual style. No Solidity contract can fetch a Wayback snapshot or weigh whether one page predates another. GenArtAuth does the crawling and the reasoning inside the contract, so the verdict and its rationale are on-chain and disputable, not a moderation team's private call.

name: GenDungeon
try_it: GenDungeon is a fully decentralized Web3 RPG built natively on GenLayer. It leverages Python Intelligent Contracts to dynamically generate unique quests, creatively evaluate user actions, and distribute rewards based on AI consensus. The frontend abandons generic crypto UIs in favor of a "Living Manuscript" aesthetic, creating an immersive storytelling experience where players interact directly with on-chain AI scribes.

name: Genetia

name: GenFortune
try_it: GenFortune is an onchain fortune cookie app powered by GenLayer's AI consensus. You open a cookie with a keyword, and GenLayer's validator network decides your fortune and rarity tier — Normal, Rare, Unique, or Legendary — with no server and no bias. Mint your fortune as a dynamic NFT and list it on GenMarket, a purpose-built marketplace for GenFortune NFTs. Built to show that GenLayer can power fun, accessible consumer apps anyone can use

name: GenHire
try_it:
GenHire is an escrow marketplace for work, built so that neither party writes the standard the work is judged by.

A client posts a brief and funds it. A freelancer proposes terms; either side can counter. When a proposal is accepted, the Intelligent Contract itself DRAFTS the binding Statement of Work turning vague wording into specific, individually checkable acceptance criteria and both parties sign that exact text by its hash before any work begins.

Everything after that is decided against the text the contract wrote. Delivered work is adjudicated by validator consensus into a completion percentage with a per-criterion breakdown, and escrow splits on that number: real work lands partly done far more often than it lands cleanly failed, so all-or-nothing is the wrong shape. "Was that in scope?" becomes a question with an on-chain answer, and out-of-scope work needs a funded change order.

No oracle, no arbitrator, no backend. One Python/GenVM contract is the whole protocol.

name: Genlayer builder companion
try_it:
Builder Companion is an AI-guided app for people building on GenLayer. It helps a user move from a rough idea to a practical project package: an Intelligent Contract, connected frontend, prototype, tests, documentation, security review, and deployment/export guidance.

name: GenLayer Content Moderator

GenLayer Content Moderator is an Intelligent Contract that performs trustless content moderation on-chain. It authenticates and ingests live content from a source URL (fetched non-deterministically inside the contract), then asks an LLM to classify it against a configurable rules policy. name: GenLayer Escrow
try_it:
GenLayer Escrow is an Intelligent Contract for agreements where payment depends on verified delivery. A client creates a job, locks GEN in escrow, and receives work as text or a URL, then approves or disputes it.
For URL disputes, validators independently verify the content and its SHA-256 digest before LLM adjudication judges the work against requirements. Unavailable or changed evidence routes to a deterministic 50/50 split instead. Jobs left unactioned past a time gate also resolve deterministically: unsubmitted jobs refund the client, submitted jobs pay the freelancer.
Useful for freelancers, clients, bounties, and contractors. Funds stay in escrow, evidence is tied to what was submitted, disputes are judged independently by multiple validators, and edge cases resolve deterministically instead of by trust — limiting reliance on a single intermediary.

name: Genlayer Gateway
try_it:
GenLayer Gateway is an interchain developer tool that brings GenLayer judgment to applications on the chain they already use.

A developer’s origin-chain contract submits a structured request containing a route ID, question or typed arguments, policy commitments, versioned evidence, callback address, nonce, and expiry. Gateway transports the request to a reviewed GenLayer Intelligent Contract, waits for the destination
result, and returns a bound result envelope to the origin chain.

The current testnet reference route starts on Base Sepolia and reaches GatewayAdjudicator on GenLayer Bradbury through the configured LayerZero V2 route.  Developers do not need to migrate their application to GenLayer or require end users to switch networks.

  Gateway is designed for multiple reviewed GenLayer contracts. Each route binds a destination contract, allowed method, argument schema, result schema, authorization model, replay protection, failure semantics, and trust disclosure.

name: GenLayer RL Agent Autonomy: reinforcement learning against on-chain LLM-consensus rewards
try_it:
The project demonstrates autonomous reinforcement-learning agents on GenLayer: each agent chooses actions, receives judgment-based rewards from immutable smart contracts, and updates its Q-table through the SDK.

It is for developers, researchers, and evaluators exploring verifiable on-chain AI and agent learning.

It is useful because it makes the full learning loop inspectable. From action selection and contract evaluation to reward consumption and policy updates, while preventing the agent from changing the rules it is judged by.

name: GenMeme Guard — AI Rug Inspector & Smart Money Radar
try_it:
Static scanners hand out 100/100 scores to worthless micro-caps. GenMeme Guard replaces that with an audit that must survive independent re-execution by multiple validators before it is stored on chain.

Each validator fetches its own evidence — DEXScreener market data, RugCheck authority and distribution metrics — runs its own LLM audit, and the results must reach equivalence before anything is written. The caller supplies nothing: the telemetry argument is ignored, because a caller able to fill gaps left by an incomplete upstream response would be deciding its own verdict, and every validator reading that payload would agree perfectly.

Equivalence covers every field stored and displayed, not just the score: verdict, scale tier, both authority flags and the unverified-metrics list must match exactly.

Evidence outranks the model. A live mint or freeze authority forces a critical verdict. A metric nothing could back is stored as unknown, never as a reassuring zero.

name: GenOracle
try_it:
GenOracle is a prediction market dApp where users create YES/NO markets and bet with demo G-USD. Each market locks an authoritative source domain before betting begins. After the deadline, anyone can submit official evidence from that domain. GenLayer AI validators independently render and interpret the evidence, then reach consensus on YES or NO. The contract deterministically settles the market and lets winning bettors claim their proportional share of the pool.

GenOracle is designed for markets whose outcomes require interpreting real-world information that deterministic smart contracts cannot evaluate on their own.

name: GenShield
try_it:
Onchain insurance has never had a custody problem. It has a specification problem. A payout condition must be encoded as a parametric trigger long before anyone knows what the failure will look like, so cover either fires on events that were not really losses or misses the loss that happened. Fixing that by importing judgment from off-chain puts back the thing on-chain insurance was meant to remove: a party who decides.

GenShield keeps the coverage wording in plain language and makes the wording itself the settlement logic. An underwriter opens a product with the wording and the hosts whose reporting counts as evidence. LPs fund the risk pool and take premium; policyholders buy cover priced off a per-day rate and pool utilisation.

When a claim is filed, the contract gathers its own evidence receipts from the insured chain, incident reporting from the allowlisted hosts and reads it against the wording under GenVM consensus. There is no resolver key.

name: GenSignal: AI Trading Signal Terminal
try_it:
GenSignal is a decentralized AI trading intelligence terminal built on GenLayer. It bridges real-time quantitative crypto market indicators (Binance 4H OHLCV) with GenVM Intelligent Contracts to generate verifiable, consensus-backed trading signals.

Targeted at crypto traders, quant analysts, and autonomous DeFi agents, GenSignal eliminates single-LLM hallucination risk through GenLayer's Equivalence Principle: a leader node generates structured trade theses across 8 strategy desks (RSI/EMA, SMC, Order Blocks, Liquidity Sweeps), and 5 independent validator nodes verify verdict alignment and confidence thresholds before finalizing on-chain.

Key Features:
- 5-Validator Multi-LLM Consensus on GenVM
- Non-custodial EIP-712 / x402 Micropayment verification
- 14 real-time quantitative momentum, volume, and volatility metrics
- Tamper-proof on-chain record & transparent verification explorer

name: GenWork v3.0 - AI-Powered Decentralized Escrow & Job Marketplace (Fully Secured)
try_it:
GenWork is a Web3 freelance job marketplace built on GenLayer that removes the need for centralized escrow agents. Clients can post jobs by defining explicit acceptance criteria (up to 8 rules) and locking GEN tokens in the smart contract. Freelancers submit authenticated evidence (strictly HTTPS/IPFS URLs) to prove their work.
To ensure 100% fund conservation and prevent arbitrary payouts, GenWork employs a strict state machine. When the AI validator approves a submission, funds are not released immediately. Instead, the job enters a "CHALLENGE_WINDOW" with a live on-chain countdown. During this hold period, the client can either accept the work to release the escrow early or submit counter-evidence to dispute the AI's decision. If the window expires without a dispute, anyone can trigger the final payout. This guarantees complete deliverable provenance and secure dispute resolution.

name: Get a Medical Second Opinion
try_it:
Second Opinion is a non-binding medical second opinion built as a GenLayer Intelligent Contract. A person connects a wallet and submits a structured, anonymous case — age, sex, symptoms, history, current diagnosis and treatment, and optionally a doctor's report as text.

A jury of independent LLM validators reaches consensus on three on-chain outputs:

Plausibility of the diagnosis — PLAUSIBLE, QUESTIONABLE, or INSUFFICIENT_DATA (NO_DIAGNOSIS if none entered)
Urgency of a specialist referral — URGENT, MODERATE, or ROUTINE
A written assessment — possible explanations, what it means, next steps, and treatment to discuss with a doctor

The point of GenLayer here is trust: not one hidden model's guess, but a finding a panel of different models independently agreed was defensible.

name: GNS — GenLayer Naming Service
try_it:
Readable names for the intelligent contract economy. GNS lets wallets, contracts, AI agents, apps, and project teams register .gen names on GenLayer, attach profile records, create subnames, and use GenLayer's validator network for AI-assisted identity and dispute review.

GNS is a GenLayer-native naming registry. Simple registry actions such as registration, renewal, and record updates are deterministic. Subjective trust decisions such as name review, report review, and project verification go through comparative AI consensus via the Equivalence Principle. Identity verification is handled by the separate TrustSeal contract — GNS reads proof-health data from it to display verification badges on name profiles.

name: GNS - Genlayer Naming Service
try_it:
GNS is a naming and identity layer built on GenLayer. It lets wallets, contracts, AI agents, apps and project teams register readable .gen names, attach profile and project records, create subnames, configure primary addresses and use reverse lookup from wallet addresses back to names.

Registry state lives directly in the GenLayer contract rather than a backend database. name: Governancefork
try_it: Governance Fork replaces the up/down DAO vote with a lineage of proposals. A DAO imports a real governance proposal; the proposer submits an intent envelope (objective, scope, constraints, mutable vs immutable dimensions); community evidence — real web pages — is fetched on-chain via gl.nondet.web.render and frozen; then GenLayer validators reach semantic consensus, via gl.eq_principle.prompt_comparative, on whether the envelope faithfully represents the proposal. Anyone can then fork a faithful proposal into a new version that keeps the intent and declares its delta, or challenge a verdict to trigger re-adjudication instead of casting a vote. Every action is backed by a native GEN bond with a deterministic, replay-safe settlement. Built for DAOs, delegates, and communities who want disagreement to produce a concrete alternative instead of a rejected proposal.

name: GovSentry
try_it: GovSentry is an autonomous on-chain governance firewall built natively on GenVM to intercept malicious DAO proposal takeovers, stealth parameter tampering, and treasury drain exploits.

name: GrantAuditor
try_it:
GrantAuditor is a decentralized milestone escrow and adjudication protocol built on the GenLayer network. It eliminates the need for human committees, political favoritism, and oracle latency by leveraging GenLayer's Nondeterministic AI Consensus.

Who is it for? DAOs, grant programs, freelancers, and protocol foundations who want secure, trustless milestone-based token payouts.

What makes it useful? Instead of relying on multi-sigs or manual review boards, GrantAuditor uses GenVM's web rendering capabilities and LLM consensus to automatically verify GitHub pull requests, documents, and deliverables against stored criteria. It features an unbreakable on-chain escrow system with a 4-outcome verdict engine (RELEASE, PARTIAL, CUT, ESCALATE). If source files fail to render, the AI safely triggers an ESCALATE status, preserving funds for a fallback DAO Human Arbitration Panel to step in. It is a fully autonomous and secure infrastructure for decentralized work.

name: GrantGate
try_it: GrantGate turns software-grant milestones into verifiable on-chain decisions. A sponsor freezes a builder, public GitHub repository, deadline, and up to five measurable criteria before evidence exists. The assigned builder submits one canonical commit URL. GenLayer validators render that immutable commit and classify every criterion as MET, NOT_MET, or INSUFFICIENT; the contract derives ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or UNRESOLVED and stores the explanation. GrantGate is for grant sponsors and builders who should not control their own outcome. Solidity cannot independently read an unstructured commit page and reach semantic consensus about whether the work satisfies written criteria. GrantGate uses GenLayer for that decision and fails safely when evidence is unavailable or contradictory. Studionet uses simulated GEN and this Explorer entry is Preview.

name: GrantJudge
try_it:
GrantJudge is a weighted grant evaluation protocol for DAOs. A treasurer deposits a GEN pool and publishes weighted criteria in plain English. Proposers submit proposals and stake a spam deposit.

GenLayer is used only for semantic interpretation: reading a proposal against a criterion. Brackets, weighted totals, rankings, proportional splits and transfers are deterministic integer arithmetic.

Before any model runs, the contract computes a bracket per criterion. The model chooses inside it. A proposal that never addresses a criterion cannot score above 2/7. A contest must add novel text — verbatim resends are refused before scoring.

Eight outcomes on studio-dev: funded, partially funded, qualified, rejected, contested and won, contested and lost, cancelled, stalled.

name: Guild Passport: Portable Consent-First Credential Registry

name: MolfGraph
try_it:
MolfGraph checks whether a legal finding holds up somewhere else.

The problem: legal research is asserted, not verified. Someone says two rulings agree, cites a government page, and you have to take it on trust. The page can change later and the citation silently rots.

MolfGraph fixes both halves. A study is registered as an immutable, hashed version that can never be edited, only corrected by appending a new one. Evidence is pinned to the SHA-256 of the source as fetched, so if a publisher edits the page, verification fails loudly instead of passing quietly.

Claims about how two studies relate are never taken at face value. GenLayer validators re-fetch the evidence, re-read it, and decide. An edge appears only if they agree.

To use it: open the site, create a local StudioNet account (auto-funded), press Register sample pack, then Adjudicate sample claims. An accepted edge appears on the Live graph with the digest that backed it.

name: MyoGen: Decentralized AI-Powered Muscle Physiology Explorer on GenLayer
try_it:

If accepted, the term is permanently added to the dictionary, and the user earns a 2x GEN reward. If rejected, the stake is burned. This creates a cryptoeconomic incentive for scientific accuracy and perfectly showcases the power of GenLayer's non-deterministic AI validators to perform complex fact-checking entirely on-chain.

name: NDA Sentinal

The violator has a 7-day appeal window. Every appeal declares one enum ground (PRIOR_DISCLOSURE, ATTRIBUTION_ERROR, KEYWORD_MISMATCH) and cites an evidence URL the appellate jury also fetches on-chain. name: OATH — Claim Verification Protocol

adjudicate() records only a PROVISIONAL verdict and never touches trust or stake; appeals are priced off the original stake (×2, then ×4), and re-adjudication overwrites the provisional result.
