name: PolicyVault
try_it:
PolicyVault is a GenLayer governance dApp for turning natural-language treasury policies into enforceable on-chain spending rules. Validators use AI consensus to interpret policy text and compile canonical rules such as allowed categories, prohibited uses, budget caps, and approval requirements.

After a policy version is accepted and activated, each spend request is classified by validators and resolved deterministically by the contract as ALLOWED, DENIED_CATEGORY, DENIED_CAP, or NEEDS_APPROVAL. Approved decisions update persistent budget and category accounting, while denied requests leave accounting unchanged.

The live app demonstrates infrastructure spending, prohibited speculative assets, marketing caps, and related-party approval routing with a full on-chain audit trail.

name: PolyglotVault
try_it:
PolyglotVault is an autonomous AI-adjudicated subtitle & video localization escrow dApp on GenLayer. Creators lock GEN bounties for video translation while GenLayer's on-chain AI consensus autonomously parses transcripts against submitted subtitle files (.srt/.vtt) to settle payouts, enforce cultural tone & specialized quiz criteria, or slash spam.
Key Highlights:
1. Native AI Consensus: Evaluates non-deterministic media nuance & custom film quiz criteria on-chain via gl.nondet.web.render.
2. Anti-Spam Staking & Slashing: Translators lock 20% stake; missing 48h deadlines triggers automated slashing.
3. 24h Cooling-Off & Dispute: Supports raise_dispute transition blocking finalization for arbitration.

name: Prediction Market — AI-resolved multi-option markets
try_it:
AI-resolved multi-option prediction markets on GenLayer. Anyone creates a market with a question, 2-8 options, 1-3 authoritative source URLs, and an ISO deadline by locking a 5 GEN deposit. Bettors escrow GEN on an option. After the deadline, anyone triggers resolution: the contract fetches the locked sources and AI-validator consensus settles outcome, summary, confidence, source authority. Winners split the pool parimutuel-style; INVALID refunds all and forfeits the deposit; no-winner refunds all and returns the deposit.

Betting/resolution horizon enforced on-chain (GenVM datetime.now): deadlines must be future ISO, bets close at the deadline, resolution refused before it; time and deadline feed the adjudication context.

For bettors and traders who want outcomes settled by neutral AI consensus instead of a platform that holds escrow: no trusted intermediary, live-data settlement, on-chain deadlines, reusable frontend. Live: https://qlxjcj.github.io/genlayer-prediction-market-v2/

name: Presnce is AI-Verified Event Attendance
try_it: Presnce replaces fake-able check-ins (POAP claims without attendance, shareable QR codes, centralized EventBrite lists) with AI-verified proof. Attendees submit a public URL a tweet posted at the event, a venue photo, or an RSVP confirmation. The platform fetches that URL directly and five independent AI validators judge whether the proof is real, returning a verdict (valid / insufficient / invalid) with a confidence score, stored permanently on-chain. Valid claims mint a free attendance certificate NFT, shareable to X as a 1200×630 PNG. Organizers create events for 0.01 GEN; attendees claim for 0.005 GEN (anti-spam, non-refundable).

name: Prior Art Court
try_it:
Prior Art Court settles copying disputes on-chain. A complainant stakes a bond and points at two URLs — the original and the alleged copy — under a published category. The contract fetches both pages from the live web itself, applies that category's doctrine, and returns one of four verdicts: INFRINGING, DERIVATIVE_FAIR, INDEPENDENT, or EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE. Consensus is on the verdict, not the wording — validators who agree the works are similar but split on the outcome do not pass. The loser's bond pays the winner; cases that cannot be decided safely escalate to a three-source appeal that settles which work came first.

For journalists, open-source maintainers, and platforms who now rely on a moderation queue or DMCA form: a court where the standard is public, the judge cannot be lobbied, and the reasoning is on-chain.

The judgement is subjective, the evidence must be read at judgement time, and money is on it. GenLayer is where all three hold at once.

name: PromiseLedger
try_it: PromiseLedger is a decentralized oracle for public commitments (roadmaps, policy changes, etc.). Users register a promise alongside a public evidence URL. The Intelligent Contract fetches the page and evaluates progress via AI consensus, assigning a status (FULFILLED, IN_PROGRESS, BROKEN, UNVERIFIABLE) along with a verbatim citation. It features a deterministic dispute mechanism to check if the evidence page has changed, and enforces deadlines off-prompt. The frontend is a seamless Vite/React app powered by genlayer-js.

name: Proof Bounty
try_it:
Proof Bounty lets a creator lock a GEN reward against a precommitted, immutable claim and proof criteria. Any number of challengers can accept and race to submit evidence. Once evidence is submitted, the Intelligent Contract fetches the URL itself, live, inside GenVM, and asks independent GenLayer validators to judge only the fetched content, never the challenger's own description of it. Consensus requires every validator's verdict to agree before a payout happens.

Five outcomes are possible: approved, partial (a bucketed percentage), rejected, needs revision, or insufficient evidence, each mapped to a specific escrow transition. Disputes route to a named arbiter, but that ruling never moves money directly. It always settles through a second, independent round of GenLayer consensus, so no human ever holds final authority over a payout once evidence has been judged.

name: ProofFlow — Verify Actions. Trigger Outcomes.
try_it: ProofFlow is a programmable proof-of-action platform powered by GenLayer Intelligent Contracts. Campaign creators define a verifiable action and the outcome that should occur when it is completed. Participants submit transaction proof, while GenLayer validators independently evaluate evidence from separate data sources and reach consensus on PASS or FAIL. ProofFlow binds participant identity and verification timing to contract-derived context, reducing reliance on user-supplied claims. When verification passes, the Intelligent Contract stores the result and automatically triggers the campaign’s one-time programmable outcome. The current V2.2 MVP supports Ethereum Sepolia actions, with an architecture designed to expand to quests, rewards, credentials, bounties, grants, access control, education, and other verifiable workflows.

name: PROOFMARK
try_it:
Proofmark covers agent work. A buyer backs a job an agent promised to deliver by a deadline; LPs fund per-tier pools, the premium is a fixed percent of coverage, and if nothing is delivered the contract pays the buyer.

Judgment runs on real evidence. A spec is a link to one exact version of a file on GitHub (a 40-character commit id) plus its SHA-256. Only the agent's wallet can attach a deliverable, and the contract re-opens that link, refusing any bytes that do not hash to the commitment. No deliverable by the deadline is a deterministic breach, nothing to game. Otherwise validators re-fetch both files and score conformance.

The mechanics stay honest: the agent posts a bond of at least the coverage when it accepts, and a breach pays the buyer out of that bond, never LP capital. A claim posts a 2 GEN bond, refunded if it holds, forfeited if not. One wallet binds one agent; a job's owner cannot insure it. Reputation is only as strong as the wallet behind it, a real limit.

name: ProofOfShip
try_it: ProofOfShip is a trust-minimized software delivery adjudication app built on GenLayer. A client locks a public GitHub repository, builder, deadline, and explicit acceptance criteria. The builder accepts those immutable terms and submits evidence bound to an exact commit SHA. Neither party, the frontend, nor a backend can choose the verdict. The Intelligent Contract validates authorization, state transitions, evidence provenance, replay domains, and asks GenLayer validators to semantically determine whether every criterion is demonstrated. The on-chain result is ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or fail-closed UNRESOLVED when evidence or consensus is insufficient. The responsive frontend connects directly through genlayer-js and distinguishes wallet state, pending finalization, execution success, error, and authoritative readback. No token, stake, escrow, payout, or backend is used.

name: ProofPatch
try_it: ProofPatch is a GenLayer-native semantic upgrade firewall for Intelligent Contracts. It protects protocols, DAOs, and contract teams from unsafe or weakly-evidenced upgrades by freezing the exact candidate bytes and binding them to immutable source, CI, and independent audit evidence. Validators independently review the evidence and policy requirements, and only exact finalized agreement can authorize installation—there is no fuzzy confidence threshold. Repair, retry, expiry, reconciliation, and timeout paths prevent funds or upgrade state from remaining locked indefinitely. The production app reads live Bradbury state, connects wallets, preflights evidence, tracks returned transaction hashes, and displays consensus, finality/lifecycle, and GenVM execution separately. The canonical v1.0.0 → v2.0.0 upgrade completed on Bradbury as VERIFIED / INSTALL_VERIFIED.

name: ProofSponsor
try_it: ProofSponsor lets sponsors define qualitative campaign requirements and lets creators submit public deliverable evidence tied to their wallet through a campaign-specific proof marker. GenLayer validators decide whether the accessible evidence meaningfully satisfies the campaign requirements and contains the expected wallet attribution. APPROVED evidence is recorded in an onchain claim registry so the same evidence cannot be reused by another wallet. The app is permissionless: reviewers can create their own campaigns and test both APPROVED and REJECTED paths without funding.

name: QuantumSafeScan Lite
try_it: QuantumSafeScan Lite helps developers, security reviewers, and open-source teams assess a public GitHub repository's visible security and post-quantum readiness. Connect a wallet, enter a repository URL, and the Bradbury Intelligent Contract renders the repository and security-policy pages. Validators use comparative consensus to normalize evidence about README and disclosure policies, legacy cryptography, possible secret indicators, and PQC/ML-KEM/ML-DSA readiness. The contract calculates and stores a 0–100 score, LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH risk level, evidence summary, verdict, and three recommended fixes. Results remain readable by wallet and scan ID, providing an auditable on-chain snapshot without a centralized analysis backend. Public evidence only; this is a lightweight readiness assessment, not a substitute for a professional code audit.

name: QUORUM
try_it:
Most oracles read one source and hand back a number. If that source is wrong, stale, or interested, nothing downstream can tell.

QUORUM reads several independent publishers, decides by arithmetic whether they agree, and records dissent as a first-class result. Every quotation is verified by each validator against the page it fetched itself, so nothing shown is unattested. Sources sharing a publisher are rejected at contract level, judged on the host fetched rather than anything the caller supplies.

An escrow releases funds on a corroborated verdict and returns them on a contested one. Resolve is callable by anyone, because consensus already fixed the verdict. A settlement contract records whether a single-source oracle would have acted where this one refused.

Live: nigeria-2018 corroborated at 100%; usd-eur corroborated across three rate providers; nigeria-current contested, both sources dissenting, no value published, where one source alone would have paid out on 237,527,782.

name: RecallGate
try_it: Recall Gate is a non-economic food-recall evidence registry on GenLayer Studionet. A user registers a public HTTPS listing URL, brand, product name, and at least one identifier: GTIN/UPC, lot code, or both. Baseline assessment retrieves the listing and openFDA food-enforcement data, verifies that the identifier is bound to the listing, and stores NO_ACTIVE_MATCH, QUARANTINED, or UNRESOLVED. A specific recall check stores MATCH, NO_MATCH, INVALID_OR_INACTIVE_RECALL, or UNRESOLVED. Only the registrant can activate a fresh ELIGIBLE listing. Unbound, conflicting, unreachable, stale, quarantined, unresolved, or inactive listings remain unusable. The public app supports registry inspection, signed writes, transaction finality, exact contract readback, and JSON export. Recall Gate is not FDA approval, certification, or a product-safety guarantee.

name: Redeem
try_it:
Redeem turns measurable real-world promises into escrow-backed guarantees. An issuer names a beneficiary, locks the maximum liability, and freezes the guarantee terms, approved HTTPS evidence sources, authority roles, outcome classes, payout matrix, and claim deadline. 

When a redemption is opened, GenLayer validators independently inspect the frozen public evidence and reach consensus on one precommitted outcome code. The AI never decides how much money to pay. Deterministic contract logic maps the agreed outcome to the payout fixed at creation. Results are provisional before settlement, allowing either party to challenge with a 5% bond and trigger a second review under the same frozen rules. 

Source failures and inconclusive reviews use bounded retry and refund paths rather than silently denying claims. Redeem has no admin settlement authority, claimant-added evidence authority, backend judge, or arbitrary model-selected payout.

name: Regulatory Edition Applicability Lock
try_it: Regulatory Edition Applicability Lock records which FAA Order JO 7400.11 edition applies to a Title 14 CFR Part 71 §71.1 activity date. A case owner freezes the date and designation family, then GenLayer validators independently retrieve dated eCFR text and Federal Register records, compare consequential facts, and write a conclusive or fail-closed result on Studionet. The result preserves official authority documents, effective dates, retry state, successor lineage, and downstream checklist bindings. It is built for aviation operations, compliance teams, and auditors who need a reviewable regulatory baseline rather than a manually selected edition. GenLayer is essential because external web retrieval and validator consensus occur inside the Intelligent Contract before state changes; a conventional client or server could not provide the same decentralized decision boundary.

name: ReleaseProof — Software Release Verification with GenLayer Consensus
try_it:
ReleaseProof is a GenLayer application for verifying whether a specific software commit or release satisfies user-defined requirements.

Each review is bound to a full immutable Git commit SHA instead of mutable HEAD or branch content. GenLayer validators independently inspect commit-pinned GitHub evidence and reach consensus on VERIFIED, FAILED, or INCONCLUSIVE.

When criteria depend on release integrity, ReleaseProof conditionally evaluates commit-specific CI checks, release/tag relationships, artifacts, checksums, and signature evidence. Missing or ambiguous required evidence cannot produce VERIFIED.

The app is designed for builders, auditors, grant programs, and teams that need reproducible software verification without relying on a single reviewer.

name: Remedy — Consensus Security Settlement (V2)
try_it: Remedy is a consensus security-settlement protocol on GenLayer. Projects fund bug-bounty campaigns against a commit-pinned contract; researchers submit claims with locked evidence. GenLayer validators read the canonical claim straight from the vault, judge it against the exact source (hashed and recorded, never truncated), and drive one of five outcomes: Reward, Reject, HoldForPatch, MergeDuplicate, or Escalate. Settlement is permissionless: the vault reads the verdict directly from the verifier and pays from its own on-chain schedule, so no owner, project, or caller supplies the outcome or amount. A verdict-bound claim cannot be dismissed, and held escrow can only be released once a re-review verifies the fix. Every outcome, including the dissenting minority view, is recorded on-chain, and a real-contract test suite proves each guard.

name: ReplicaStake
try_it:
Roughly 70% of published computational results do not reproduce, and peer review never runs the code. ReplicaStake makes that falsifiable.

An author stakes credits behind exactly one number from their paper - one cell of one table - together with the protocol needed to get it and a repo pinned to a commit SHA. A replicator runs the experiment off-chain in public CI and posts the log. The Intelligent Contract then fetches that evidence itself and makes three judgments no deterministic chain and no oracle can make: did the run follow the declared protocol, what number did it actually produce, and is the gap defensible inside the declared tolerance?

REPRODUCED keeps the stake and marks the claim. FAILED sends 70% of it to the replicator. INVALID_ATTEMPT costs a sloppy challenger half their bond and leaves the author untouched - that third verdict is what stops this being a griefing machine.

For researchers, reviewers, funders, and anyone tired of taking a table on faith.

name: REPROVE
try_it:
REPROVE is a GenLayer-native protocol for trustworthy scientific replication. Study creators preregister a claim, replication method, evidence requirements, outcome rule, and reward before results are known. Researchers then open a replication attempt, publish typed public evidence, and submit a reported result.

GenLayer validators independently retrieve and assess the same evidence through consensus. The protocol stores a bounded outcome—REPLICATED, FAILED_TO_REPLICATE, PROTOCOL_DEVIATION, or INCONCLUSIVE—together with deterministic evidence-window hashes. This makes the result auditable and binds the consensus decision to the exact evidence representation that was evaluated.

REPROVE includes study registration, evidence validation, finalized evaluation, public archive records, creator-funded rewards, researcher withdrawals, and closed-study lifecycle controls.

name: Research Artifact Integrity Covenant
try_it:
Research Artifact Integrity Covenant helps researchers, curators, and reviewers inspect evidence behind a registered research-artifact set. Register exact DataCite DOIs, Zenodo records, or GitHub commits; GenLayer validators fetch public evidence and agree on identity, access, version alignment, and license declarations. The contract stores per-artifact decisions and derives READY, DEGRADED, UNRESOLVED, or BLOCKED.

Anyone may propose a successor, but only the active predecessor's authority can approve it as canonical. The public app supports registration, approval, assessment, and transaction recovery. Browse includes a READY example and an explicitly labeled negative test fixture that reaches BLOCKED for a mismatched relationship.

GenLayer supplies consensus over changing external evidence instead of a verdict chosen by the app server. This Studionet Preview does not establish DOI ownership, scientific correctness, reproducibility, or legal validity.

name: RetractionDependency
try_it:
RetractionDependency is a GenLayer Studionet research-dependency auditor for people and systems that rely on published evidence. A proposal owner freezes an exact claim and its DOI/PMID dependencies. Crossref and Europe PMC supply correction or retraction evidence, while GenLayer validators independently assess whether each notice is bound to the cited paper and materially removes support for the frozen claim.

The consensus verdict is stored by the Intelligent Contract and directly changes the proposal state: USABLE evidence can make it ELIGIBLE and then ACTIVE; unresolved evidence remains in EVIDENCE_HOLD; any INVALID_FOR_CLAIM dependency makes it INVALIDATED. Permissionless later reviews, replay protection, conservative accepted-history derivation, and transaction readback prevent a newer usable result or transient source failure from erasing an established invalidation. The public demo includes one ACTIVE positive case and two INVALIDATED cases.

name: Reverse Spec (Bounty Review and Payout Category)
try_it: Reverse Spec Bounties lets a creator post a bounty whose spec is a starting hypothesis, not a contract, along with their guess at the deeper problem worth solving. Solvers submit a rationale plus a public evidence link, no literal spec compliance required. GenLayer validators independently fetch and judge that evidence themselves at evaluation time, never trusting a solver's own description of their work, and reach consensus through tolerant equivalence rather than requiring identical output. Real GEN is escrowed at bounty creation, split 85/10/5 between winner, runner-up, and creator on finalization, and paid out through a genuine EthSend transfer into the winner's own wallet, not just recorded on an internal ledger. Abandonment recovery means close_submissions is callable by any solver with a live submission, not just the creator, so a bounty can never be permanently stranded by a creator who goes silent.

name: Review Guard
try_it:
ReviewGuard is a fake-review detector that lives inside a GenLayer Intelligent Contract. Paste any review page (an App Store listing, a Google Maps place, a product page) and the contract fetches the page on-chain with gl.nondet.web.render, then asks an LLM to grade authenticity: templated wording, copy-paste praise, bursts of similar reviews, rating-vs-text mismatch, incentivized language. It returns one of four verdicts (TRUSTWORTHY, MIXED, SUSPICIOUS, UNRESOLVABLE), a 0-100 trust score, and concrete red flags, all stored on-chain. A URL cache means repeat lookups are free view calls.

Consensus checks meaning, not shape. The nondet block runs inside gl.eq_principle.prompt_comparative — validators agree the verdicts match and trust scores are close, so two validators reaching different verdicts cannot both pass. A regular smart contract cannot fetch a web page or reason about writing. Remove the web read and the LLM and nothing remains.

name: Rigor
try_it:
Rigor is a bounty market for genuine flaws in scientific papers. A sponsor funds a bounty on a
real arXiv paper, and anyone can stake GEN to submit a written critique of a flaw. A judged
critique returns the stake, rewards the hunter, or slashes it — automatically, with no admin in
the loop.

Judgment is consensus over live evidence. To resolve a critique, validators each independently
fetch the paper's live full text from arXiv, see the exact passage the critique challenges, and
vote on whether it is substantive. Only their agreement moves money — no single model decides.

Anti-gaming is built in: a critique commits as a hash and reveals later, verified byte-for-byte.
Resolution needs five commit-rounds and five distinct wallets staking at least 1 GEN on a
different paper, and the reward is capped at what those wallets parked, so a fake crowd cannot
pay for itself. Huge papers are judged around the hunter's verbatim quote, never truncated.

name: SaleProof
try_it:
Sale Proof helps shoppers test whether a merchant’s advertised discount is genuine. Merchants register a public product URL, lock a bond, and announce a reference price and discount. Watchers record validator-checked page prices in an on-chain history. A buyer can challenge a sale; validators compare the live page with the frozen pre-sale history and return GENUINE, INFLATED_REFERENCE, DECEPTIVE, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with confidence and reasoning. The verdict can be appealed once, then settlement returns deposits or compensates the buyer from the merchant bond and records strikes.

It is for shoppers, merchants, and marketplace communities that need an auditable way to test discount claims. GenLayer is required because validators must read changing web pages, reason over historical evidence, agree on a subjective verdict, and commit that result on-chain.

name: ScopeFlow
try_it: ScopeFlow is a GenLayer project for controlling changes to an agreed project scope. A creator establishes the baseline scope, then new change requests are evaluated by GenLayer validators as IN_SCOPE, SCOPE_EXTENSION, or NEEDS_CLARIFICATION. The semantic verdict is stored onchain and drives deterministic workflow state, preventing ambiguous changes from silently becoming part of the project.

name: ScopeSeal Accord
try_it: ScopeSeal Accord is for procurement sponsors and contractors who need a neutral decision when an official contract amendment may change the agreed scope. The parties co-ratify an immutable baseline and fund 2 GEN. GenLayer validators fetch the exact official TED original and modification notices, compare their meaning, and finalize either contractor release, bilateral negotiation, or a non-penalizing retryable result. Deterministic contract checks control every GEN consequence. This Preview deployment proves the product on Studionet; it does not claim legal advice, physical-performance proof, production adoption, or another network.

name: ScoreSettle — Sports Score Settlement Intelligent Contract
try_it: ScoreSettle lets two parties agree on a sports score outcome (e.g. total goals over/under a threshold) and settle it trustlessly. party_a and party_b are bound to real signing wallets, never free-text names. resolve_agreement can only be called in a 24-hour window after the agreed full-time and requires at least two independent, reputable sports sources to agree on the final score before producing a verdict. The voting source set locks only once real, fixture-matched evidence is found, preventing anyone from permanently poisoning an agreement with irrelevant pages. Includes a full test suite (167 offline tests) and a live frontend.

name: Sentinel
try_it:
Sentinel turns an SLA into an enforceable, self auditing bond. A seller posts a covenant, a spec, a live endpoint, and a real GEN bond, instead of just a promise on a dashboard.

Anyone can trigger an audit at any time. GenLayer validators independently fetch the seller's live endpoint and judge it against the advertised spec under the Equivalence Principle, no validator sees or trusts the seller's own reporting. 
A single bad audit changes nothing; only three consecutive confirmed violations trigger a breach, which automatically slashes the bond and pays it out to registered beneficiaries. Every outcome is fail closed: an unreachable endpoint is recorded as inconclusive, never silently scored as compliant.

It's for anyone who currently has to take an API provider, oracle, or service operator's word for their uptime or behavior, freelance infra, agent to agent service agreements, or any B2B SLA where the buyer has no way to independently verify performance today. Sentinel replaces

name: Shipyard
try_it: Shipyard is a developer platform for builders creating applications on GenLayer. It simplifies project creation, smart contract deployment, discovery, and verification, while helping users explore public projects and understand who built them. With wallet-based sign-in, public profiles, and a cleaner mobile experience, Shipyard makes building and engaging with GenLayer applications more accessible, transparent, and trustworthy.

name: Skill Badge
try_it:
SkillBadge is a credential dapp on GenLayer's StudioNet. You pick a skill (python, typescript, solidity...), point at a public GitHub repo that proves it, and the network's validators actually fetch that URL, read what's there, and judge whether the repo backs the claim. The verdict is VERIFIED at bronze, silver, or gold, or REJECTED, with a written reason that stays on-chain.

It's for developers who want proof of what they can do: job applicants, open-source contributors, communities that hand out skill-based roles. Claims and verifications are free and gasless, so there's no money in the contract and nothing to game for profit.

What makes it useful is that the proof is earned, not just claimed. Anyone can say they know TypeScript, here a neutral validator network reads the actual code first. Everything is transparent. the reason behind each verdict is public, and a rejected claim can be retried with better evidence until it verifies.

name: SkillSlot Clearing : Validator-Cleared Agent Access
try_it:
SkillSlot Clearing is a wallet-enabled GenLayer marketplace for capacity-constrained AI-agent access. Providers bond 1 GEN to offers backed by authenticated agent metadata, while requesters escrow 1 GEN with exact needs, capability IDs, and exclusions. GenLayer validators inspect the bounded offer/request graph and decide semantic compatibility; deterministic contract code creates one-time route grants, credits matched providers, refunds unmatched deposits, and enables permissionless recovery of expired locked funds.
Use SkillSlot when keyword matching is too weak for scarce access allocation and you need validator-controlled decisions with transparent, onchain accounting.

name: SkyVerdict
try_it:
SkyVerdict is parametric flight-delay insurance with no trusted oracle and no claims desk. Buy coverage — a plain form, a multi-flight trip in one purchase, or a plain-English description and once the flight lands, independent GenLayer validators each fetch live tracker pages on their own, extract a structured verdict, and reach Optimistic-Democracy consensus. Payout transfers automatically in the same transaction; if validators can't agree, the contract fails closed (NO_QUORUM) rather than guessing.

Built to showcase GenLayer's real differentiators: multi-source median aggregation resistant to a single hallucinated outlier, natural-language policy creation where the model only extracts into a schema the contract independently validates, and a Reasoning Explorer showing the real math behind every verdict. An optional fault classifier (airline vs. weather/ATC) is informational-only, never touching payout. Every method is directly agent-callable via a published skill manifest.

name: SnakeChain: Proof of Play
try_it:
PROOF OF PLAY is an on-chain activity engine built as a classic Snake game on the GenLayer Studionet testnet.  

Every meaningful action—movement and eating apples—is treated as a blockchain transaction. Players connect a Rabby wallet, and the game records scores on-chain (every 5 apples), generates a cryptographically signed replay hash on death, and uses GenLayer’s AI-powered Intelligent Contracts to classify the player’s play style based on performance.  

It is a working demo that demonstrates how gameplay can serve as decentralized, unmanipulable proof of skill, activity, and style.

name: SoulStamp
try_it: SoulStamp is a GenLayer-powered identity proof health protocol that links wallets to public GitHub, X, and Discord identities. Users prove control of an account using public verification evidence or an OAuth-backed Discord attestation, while GenLayer validators independently evaluate the evidence and reach consensus on the result. Verified proofs are stored with structured dossiers containing proof strength, risk band, confidence, canonical identity data, and supporting evidence. SoulStamp can later reverify existing proofs against live public evidence and update their health to ACTIVE, STALE, REVOKED, CONFLICTED, or FLAGGED, creating an auditable history of identity changes over time

name: SourceSeal: Consensus-Backed Claim Verifier
try_it: SourceSeal turns public web evidence into a verifiable on-chain verdict. A user submits a claim with one to three HTTPS sources. The Intelligent Contract fetches those pages inside GenVM, classifies the claim as SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, and asks independent validators to check the result against the same evidence. Only a consensus-accepted result is stored as a queryable record. It is built for communities, researchers, markets, and AI agents that need an auditable decision instead of trusting one model.

name: Soyara
try_it:
Soyara is an agentic DEX on GenLayer Bradbury. Users express trading intent in natural language, while an agent swarm parses the request, obtains live liquidity quotes, selects a route, and prepares the trade for consensus validation.

Unlike conventional AI trading, agents cannot settle trades unilaterally. Proposals are validated through GenLayer Optimistic Democracy, and the consensus verdict is authenticated by the enforced settlement path before execution. AgentExecutor binds execution to the exact approved parameters, including user, tokens, amounts, recipient, route, and fees. Modified parameters and replayed authorizations are rejected.

The Soyara SDK exposes the same consensus validation and authenticated settlement pipeline to developers building autonomous agents, preventing integrations from falling back to direct settlement.

name: StillHere
try_it:
StillHere is a romance-scam prevention protocol. A family member submits a suspect profile (public URL plus a paraphrased chat sample); the case triggers an AI jury inside the contract that fetches the profile page live and returns one of four advisory verdicts: LIKELY_REAL, INCONCLUSIVE, SUSPICIOUS, or LIKELY_SCAM_RING. The subject can file a Round 2 dispute that re-runs the jury with counter-evidence, and third parties can contribute corroborating URLs weighed on re-adjudication.

Built for adult children helping isolated parents, romance-scam recovery groups, and moderators who need a neutral second opinion before flagging a profile.

Why GenLayer: a single centralized AI cannot legally emit "LIKELY_SCAM_RING" verdicts on real people (defamation liability). GenLayer distributes the judgment across independent validator LLMs that must agree on verdict, confidence tolerance, and critical red-flag categories. No PII or chat content is stored on-chain, only keccak256 hashes.

name: SyllabusBond – Course Delivery Escrow
try_it: SyllabusBond is a decentralized tuition escrow protocol for online courses, bootcamps, and cohort programs. Organizers lock the syllabus, instructor, duration, tuition, and immutable terms before enrollment. Students then deposit tuition into the Intelligent Contract. Delivery evidence and student dispute records are evaluated by GenLayer consensus against those original commitments. Validators select a bounded outcome—delivered, materially reduced, not delivered, or evidence unavailable—while deterministic contract code controls every payout and refund. The live application reads contract totals, enrollments, verdicts, and custody outcomes directly from studionet and verifies state again after every accepted write.

name: Synquesta
try_it:
Synquesta is a GenLayer app for two kinds of play: organization quests and player-funded challenge pools.

Quests are published by brands and communities. Players answer a written brief. Validators re-run the same prompt and agree on the result. A finished win is bridged to an EVM escrow, and the player claims the reward after the grace period.

Challenges are standalone pools. A player pays entry, then pays for each answer. Every step is its own scene. Finishing adds weight to that player's share of the pool. One hour after the challenge ends, the escrow settles and finishers claim their share.

Both paths keep the outcome on-chain instead of in a spreadsheet: the intelligent contract decides, the bridge delivers, and the escrow pays.

name: TalentVerify
try_it: TalentVerify lets a wallet submit a claimed programming skill, a GitHub username, and one to three public repository URLs. Its GenLayer Intelligent Contract fetches bounded public GitHub metadata, language totals, and relevant manifest signals, then asks the leader and validators to assess the same evidence independently. The finalized on-chain record stores one of three verdicts—SUPPORTED, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, or NOT_SUPPORTED—plus a reason and evidence summary. It is designed for developers and anyone reviewing a wallet-linked skill claim. TalentVerify does not prove identity, repository ownership, code authorship, employment history, or overall hiring suitability. name: TenderDelta
try_it: TenderDelta helps bidders, contracting authorities, and public-interest monitors verify whether an ordered chain of EU TED procurement notices contains a material contract change. The frontend guides users through wallet selection, input validation, signing, consensus finality, execution checks, and authoritative contract readback. name: TenderFit
try_it: TenderFit is a GenLayer procurement marketplace where a buyer publishes a natural-language tender brief and suppliers submit proposals with prices. name: TermsRail
try_it: TermsRail is policy infrastructure for autonomous agents built on GenLayer. Users register a service with its public Terms of Service, acceptable-use and related policy sources. Agents then register a specific structured action, which TermsRail evaluates against the accepted policy snapshot to produce a canonical authorization and an execution gate. Policy changes are detected through fresh consensus, stale authorizations are invalidated, and actions must be reassessed against the current policy version. This gives agents and applications a verifiable way to check changing rules before they act rather than relying on one centralized policy interpreter.

name: TermsWatch for GenLayer
try_it: TermsWatch lets a user register a public terms or policy baseline, submit a candidate URL, and ask GenLayer validators to assess materiality, risk level, user impact, and recommended action. Each assessment is stored as a contract-generated chg_* record with source commitments, rendered snapshot hashes, accepted-write sequence, and an exportable evidence pack for steward review or downstream audits.

name: TokenScope - Multi-Chain ERC-20 Token Risk Assessment
try_it:
TokenScope scores ERC-20 token risk across four chains using Blockscout's public APIs. Validators agree on a bucketed feature vector - never on scores. Five dimensions: distribution, activity, verification, maturity, liquidity. Each score is a pure integer function of the agreed vector.

Rug pull detection is model-free: MINTABLE, PAUSABLE, HAS_BLACKLIST, UPGRADEABLE_PROXY are exact ABI method-name matches from Blockscout's structured JSON. The model controls only 3 points of 100.

Live scores: USDT/ethereum 86 (MINTABLE, PAUSABLE, HAS_BLACKLIST). PEPE/ethereum 87 (HAS_BLACKLIST). USDT0/arbitrum 88 (UPGRADEABLE_PROXY). All flags are real methods on verified contracts.

Full frontend: scan any token, explore scored tokens, compare side-by-side, view rug flags with explanations. .

name: Trade Smarter
try_it: Alpha Signal is a GenLayer app where an Intelligent Contract pulls live Binance chart data and has a validator AI jury reach consensus on a trade signal verdict, confidence, and bull/bear targets  instead of one black box deciding.

name: Treasury Copilot
try_it:
Treasury Copilot is an authorization and execution platform for AI agents that need to spend money or perform onchain actions. An owner defines what an agent may purchase, how much it may spend, which assets and recipients it may use, and what business purpose is acceptable. When the agent submits a request, deterministic controls enforce spending limits and GenLayer evaluates whether the stated intent complies with the human readable policy. Approved requests can execute using bounded wallet permissions, while denied requests never reach settlement.

Every request produces an auditable record containing its status, verdict, reasoning, and execution evidence. The current public MVP uses GenLayer for policy review, MetaMask permissions for bounded authority, 1Shot for execution, and Base Sepolia USDC

name: TRIBUNAL: Decentralized AI Escrow Court
try_it:
Tribunal allows clients and providers to lock funds in escrow. If a dispute arises over the quality or completeness of a deliverable, an AI validator jury uses GenLayer's GenVM LLM consensus to evaluate the agreement terms, deliverables, and submitted evidence, then automatically executes a verdict to refund, pay out, or split the funds.

It is designed for freelancers, clients, and Web3 collaborators who engage in subjective, contract-based work where traditional binary smart contracts are unable to judge whether the terms of an agreement were met.

What makes it useful
1. Subjective Resolution: Evaluates natural language terms directly on-chain.
2. No Human Intermediaries: Replaces slow, expensive human panels with automated AI consensus.
3. Robust Security & Safety: Solves consensus divergence using specific clock-sync hazard resolutions and validator tolerance checks.

name: TrustGate
try_it: TrustGate is a non-custodial transaction-clearance layer for people and agents. Wallets and agents often sign opaque calls without a reusable, verifiable safety decision. TrustGate binds one exact unsigned EVM transaction—including chain, sender, destination, account nonce, value, calldata, intent, policy, evidence and expiry—to an on-chain verdict. Deterministic hazards such as excessive native value, unlimited ERC-20 approvals, NFT operator approvals and malformed calldata stop immediately. When evidence requires judgment, the requester wallet sends a gasless write to a GenLayer Intelligent Contract. Independent validators fetch public sources, evaluate structured enforcement facts and finalize ALLOW, REVIEW or BLOCK through Optimistic Democracy and the Equivalence Principle. Vercel holds no private key. Humans use the dashboard; agents use the preflight/proof API and a fail-closed signing guard. Two real StudioNet proofs, full source, tests and audit evidence are public.

name: TrustGrant — Milestone Verification with GenLayer Consensus
try_it:
TrustGrant is a GenLayer application for milestone-based grants and verifiable payouts.

Grant creators define milestones, assign a named claimant, set acceptance criteria, and escrow native GEN rewards. The claimant submits public evidence, and GenLayer validators independently evaluate whether the milestone satisfies the required criteria.

Consensus produces a canonical APPROVED, REJECTED, or INCONCLUSIVE result. When a milestone is APPROVED, the escrowed reward becomes claimable only by the authorized claimant and can be paid exactly once.

TrustGrant is useful for grants, bounties, contributor programs, and other workflows where payments should depend on independently verified evidence rather than a single trusted reviewer.

name: TrustRail - Reusable AI-Arbitration Infrastructure
try_it:
TrustRail replaces the arbitration logic every dispute-resolution dApp writes from scratch. Instead of hardcoding "does this freelance deliverable match this brief," TrustRail takes your case description and evaluation criteria as deploy-time parameters — so the same contract works for freelance work, bounties, insurance claims, SLA compliance, or warranty disputes.

An initiator funds a case with real GEN. A respondent submits evidence as a public URL. GenLayer validators independently evaluate the evidence against your own criteria and reach consensus. The contract then settles automatically — real GEN transferred to the correct wallet, not just a status flag.

Proven reusable: the exact same contract, unmodified, was deployed for two unrelated domains — a coding bounty and an insurance claim — with opposite, correctly-reasoned verdicts and verified on-chain settlement to real wallets in both cases.

name: Truth Stake
try_it:
In Web3, protocol docs and governance specs often contain ambiguities leading to contested claims. Traditional oracles only provide numbers, and centralized courts pose counterparty risk.

TruthStake resolves this with an adversarial staking arena powered by GenLayer Intelligent Contracts:
1. Bonded Claim Staking: Operators stake GEN on factual/technical interpretations of protocol specs (e.g. Uniswap v4 hook bitmasks).
2. Adversarial Counter-Staking: Challengers deposit matching GEN and submit live web evidence (docs, commits, audit specs).
3. GenLayer Multi-Validator Consensus: GenVM validators independently fetch evidence (gl.nondet.web.get), compute SHA-256 byte hashes, and evaluate semantic equivalence via LLM consensus.
4. Non-Custodial Settlement: Stakes are automatically disbursed to winners on-chain with zero custodial intermediaries.

Includes a live Next.js 14 dApp on Vercel, Fastify indexer, and a 65-test security suite with SSRF and injection defenses.

name: TweetChecker is Onchain Tweet Authenticity Verification
try_it: TweetChecker detects scam patterns in tweets fake giveaways, phishing links, impersonation accounts, and other manipulation tactics common on X. You paste a tweet URL, the platform pulls the tweet's content automatically, and a decentralized network of AI validators independently scans it and reaches consensus on a verdict. The result safe, suspicious, or scam is stored permanently onchain, so no single platform, moderator, or company can alter or hide it later. There's no login and no centralized backend making the call: just a public URL in, and an immutable, publicly verifiable verdict out. Useful for checking before clicking a link, sending funds, or trusting a "verified" giveaway account.

name: Uptime Arbiter
try_it:
Uptime Arbiter is an onchain SLA-breach adjudication protocol for infrastructure providers and their customers, built on GenLayer. A provider and a customer lock GEN as escrow, and fix — at registration time, before any dispute exists — the exact public evidence sources that will ever be consulted. When the customer later claims a breach, GenLayer validators independently fetch those pinned sources themselves, compute breach-minutes, and a deterministic settlement function pays out from escrow. Either party can challenge with additional (never replacement) evidence before funds finalize.

It is not a traditional escrow platform, a prediction market, a generic dispute-resolution app, or a frontend shell around a smart contract. The core primitive is: a financially backed SLA whose breach determination depends on whether independently-fetched, precommitted public evidence sources show downtime exceeding a contractual threshold in a claimed time window.

name: UptimeBond - AI Adjudicated SLA Escrow
try_it:
UptimeBond is a decentralized SLA bond for APIs and SaaS services. A provider deposits
real GEN, names the covered customer, locks immutable service terms, and commits fixed
minor, major, and critical payout bands before coverage begins. If an incident occurs,
the customer and provider bind content-addressed monitoring, status, and response
evidence to the agreement. GenLayer validators interpret those sources against the
locked SLA and independently select one closed economic outcome. Deterministic
contract logic then pays the customer and returns any remainder to the provider
exactly once. Missing or unsafe evidence enters a bounded recovery path instead of
stranding custody.

name: VARAI
try_it:
VARAI settles football arguments people can't settle themselves — penalty or not, red card, offside, handball.

You submit the incident: competition, teams, minute, type, description, evidence. It goes to the FootballCourt Intelligent Contract on GenLayer, where validators each re-judge it independently through a fixed structure — CASE FACTS, EVIDENCE, RULE, ANALYSIS, ALTERNATIVES, VERDICT, CONFIDENCE — then vote. The verdict is what they agree on.

GenLayer is load-bearing, not decoration. One AI call is a single opinion nobody has reason to trust. Refereeing calls are disputed precisely because reasonable people disagree, so the ruling must come from independent parties converging in public. Validators compare only decision, confidence and evidence sufficiency — never prose. The consensus split is a real vote count, verifiable on-chain.

The contract returns INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rather than inventing facts, and on failure marks the case FAILED. No wallet, no betting.

name: Vector
try_it:
Vector is a verified vulnerability disclosure escrow. A sponsor stakes a bounty program against a real, live target; a researcher stakes a bond and submits a disclosure describing a vulnerability. Anyone can trigger triage: the contract fetches the live target itself, fresh, and several independent GenLayer validators each separately refetch it and reason about the claim from scratch under the Equivalence Principle, a verdict only lands once independent validators agree.

Genuine disclosures get their bond refunded plus a payout once a 48hour duplicate challenge window elapses; bad faith disclosures forfeit their bond to the pool, funding honest researchers alongside the sponsor. This is for any project that wants a bug bounty program without a centralized, conflicted triage team deciding what counts as real.

Live end to end on GenLayer Studio Devnet: deploy, register, submit, triage, and a real disclosure verified at 95% validator confidence against an actual vulnerable file, pro

name: Verda
try_it: Verda locks funding against one measurable environmental outcome, like 500 hectares restored in a named region by a deadline. The funder's deposit freezes the outcome, the money rule, and an evidence basis: the only web origins the panel may ever read. After the deadline, every GenLayer validator fetches the operator's pages itself and returns readings, never a verdict. Code inside each validator derives QUALIFIED, NOT QUALIFIED, or INCONCLUSIVE from the lowest usable independent figure and pays pro-rata. Independence is counted per publisher, not per URL. Insufficient or uncorroborated records hold the money instead of moving it, a bonded challenge re-judges the recorded bytes beside the challenger's new source, every hold has a permissionless exit, and the live contract has been driven to custody zero across eight agreements: three paid on verified impact, one refunded on a shortfall, the rest held and reclaimed.

name: Verdict
try_it: VERDICT lets two parties lock GEN as collateral over a real disagreement, submit evidence (URLs, tx references, statements), and have GenLayer's validator network independently re-fetch that evidence and reach consensus on a structured verdict, not just an outcome label but which specific evidence supports which specific claim. The GenLayer Intelligent Contract is the sole source of truth: it escrows the stake, runs the investigation, and settles the payout, so there is no off-chain adjudicator and no relay step between "decided" and "paid." It's for anyone who needs a dispute over delivery, scope, or performance resolved with real financial stakes and no human arbiter — freelance/marketplace disputes, DAO service agreements, escrow-based deals.

name: VerdictGraph
try_it: VerdictGraph is an accountability and settlement layer for autonomous multi-agent workflows. name: VeriMarket
try_it:

name: Verity
try_it: Verity is a GenLayer-powered verification layer for AI agents. It evaluates evidence and agent outputs to determine whether a claimed outcome actually happened, making agent decisions more transparent, verifiable, and trustworthy.

name: Vesting Exception Authorization Gate

name: WarrantyVault
try_it:
WarrantyVault is a decentralized application built on GenLayer that revolutionizes how hardware warranties are managed and resolved. By utilizing GenLayer's AI validators, WarrantyVault allows users to file warranty claims using natural language and direct evidence.

name: Witness Mark
try_it:
WitnessMark lets a seller lock GEN behind a specific, measurable delivery or compliance commitment, naming a buyer as beneficiary. Once the delivery window closes, the buyer submits evidence: a web-fetchable page, image, or document. A single Intelligent Contract fetches that evidence itself and reaches a verdict, FULFILLED, PARTIALLY_FULFILLED, or BROKEN, through independent leader and validator re-adjudication, then pays the stake out accordingly. Full return to the seller if terms were met, full transfer to the buyer if they weren't, a split for partial fulfillment.
This exists because in procurement, the seller paid on "fulfilled," the buyer paid on "broken," and any platform sitting between them all have directly conflicting incentives over the one judgment call that decides where real money goes. A deterministic smart contract can't make that call either, since "did this shipment match the sample" is a judgment against fetched real-world evidence, not a computation.

name: Workify Protocol

verifier. Independent validators review the evidence, reach consensus, and produce a structured verdict with a decision, score, confidence, rationale, and payout allocation.

Successful verdicts are attested back to Base for deterministic settlement. Passing work pays the worker, failed work refunds the client, and inconclusive reviews open a retry window. Appeals provide a separate review path for disputed outcomes.

Workify is useful because it combines explicit specifications, immutable evidence hashes, independent AI validator consensus
